prize_parts.citation: for showing how credit limits tied to collateral values feed back on asset prices, so that shocks to net worth are amplified and propagated into persistent fluctuations in output and investment

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged in substance: a single part for B011, credited to Kiyotaki and Moore only. The 1997 paper gives one precise dynamic general-equilibrium mechanism. Credit limits depend on collateral values, and collateral values depend on credit, so small temporary shocks become large and persistent. The mechanism is general and tractable, and nearly three decades of extension have made it a standard building block of macro-financial models. The attribution is also clean, because the originating contribution is a joint paper by exactly these two authors. Round 1 changed my wording more than my choice. I have rewritten the citation so that it names only the collateral-price feedback loop. It does not mention banks, bank runs or the external-finance-premium accelerator. That makes it explicit what is not being honoured, which the chair's questions asked for. I do not use the narrow count of explicit B011 preferences as evidence of merit. My own file is one of those counts, and Krusell, a frequent co-author, is another. The case has to stand on the mechanism, its durability and its attribution. I think it does, with the reservations below stated openly.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real and I have not talked myself out of them. First, the overlap with the 2022 prize for work on banks and financial crises (Bernanke, Diamond, Dybvig). I read the mechanisms as distinct, since one concerns bank-specific information and run dynamics and the other concerns collateral and asset-price feedback in the wider economy. A committee could still judge that financial frictions in macro have been recently honoured. Second, identification. The collateral channel is established mainly as a mechanism and a reused modelling building block, not as a measured magnitude, and the 2007-09 episode illustrates the mechanism without pinning down its size. B005 has the more direct micro-data confirmation, and I concede that point to Fredriksson, Friberg and Boppart. Third, a two-name award leaves the Gertler/Gilchrist quantitative strand uncredited. That is a cost in completeness, and I accept it in exchange for a defensible attribution line. Fourth, I am a macroeconomist, so B011 is in a field adjacent to my own and I may overrate it.

responses.point: Fredriksson prefers B005 over B011. She holds that the collateral channel is hard to identify directly, that the crisis episodes do not pin down the quantitative size of the amplification, and that the 2022 overlap weighs more heavily than my opening allowed.
responses.response: I accept the identification point and have narrowed my claim. The 2007-09 crisis is consistent with the mechanism, but it does not measure its size, and the citation should therefore credit the mechanism, not an effect. I do not accept that a theory contribution with indirect identification is a lesser kind of achievement. The prize can recognise a mechanism whose value lies in how widely it has been reused and tested in different settings, but I concede that this is a weaker kind of confirmation than the firm-level testing behind B005. On the 2022 overlap, I think it is mainly a citation-wording issue, because the 2022 work is about banks, runs and the Depression-era analysis of crises. The revised wording therefore avoids banks and the accelerator. If the committee disagrees that the two mechanisms are distinct, that would be the strongest argument for B005, and I would then want B005 argued on its own attribution terms. I cannot independently verify the empirical literatures here.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B005 first. He argues that Helpman's credit rests on the heterogeneous-firm extensions rather than on the monopolistic-competition base covered by Krugman's 2008 prize, that the citation should be anchored on selection and reallocation across firms, and that the group should stay at two names.
responses.response: This answers part of my round 1 objection. If Helpman's credit is the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple treatment of exporting versus foreign direct investment and the wider integration of firm heterogeneity into trade theory, then it is separable from the 2008 recognition, and I withdraw the suggestion that the overlap is disqualifying. The unresolved difficulty is that the marginal credit is still harder to state cleanly than for a single joint paper. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are outside the names, and Helpman's separate protection-for-sale entry (B020) adds a boundary question. Of these, I see the Bernard and Jensen exporter-premia facts as manageable through wording that credits the theory of selection, not the empirical discovery. I see Helpman's marginal credit as the point that most needs explicit committee discussion. A Melitz-centred single credit is more defensible on attribution but would understate the programme Friberg describes, so I would not prefer it to the pair. I keep B005 as my first alternative and would support the Helpman-Melitz pair with Friberg's wording if B011 does not carry.

responses.point: Boppart now prefers B005 but regards the choice as closer than his opening ranks suggested. He agrees that Kiyotaki-Moore is a clean two-author, well-confirmed contribution, and he would not add a third name to B011.
responses.response: I appreciate the candid reassessment, and I agree the two entries are close on merit. Our difference is on direct versus indirect confirmation, and I have conceded that B005 does better on it. I weigh the generality of the mechanism and the cleanness of its attribution more heavily. Both are judgments and neither is a finding. On the chair's question, I would support a two-name B011 only with a citation that separates collateral-price feedback from bank-focused and accelerator work. That wording seems to be what your reservation about overlap with B001 and 2022 needs. On B001, I agree with your own change of view: Mian-Sufi is a younger, well-identified application, and the weight of credit supply is still debated. I keep it as a second alternative for that reason and do not rank it above B011.

responses.point: Teorell prefers B012 and now regards B011 as a serious alternative, having judged that the 2022 overlap is weaker than he first thought. He accepts that the cross-country identification of constitutional and electoral-rule effects is the weakest part of his case, and that B005 and B011 have cleaner attribution.
responses.response: I am glad the overlap argument held up for you. I take your point that recent attention to institutions should not by itself count against B012, because the 2024 prize and B012 ask different questions. My concern is therefore about identification and dispersion, not about 2024. You concede that regime coding, reverse causation and the number of contributors outside the three names are the main weaknesses, and that the case should rest on the theory and later state-capacity work. A citation could be worded that way, but the field is diffuse, so the credit line is harder to draw than for B011. I list B012 below my two alternatives for that reason, but I regard it as a serious candidate. In the chair's question about a fallback, I read your answer as B011 or B005, and I note that either would fit a single-part prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that collateral-price amplification is distinct from the banks-and-crises work recognised in 2022. If it does not, the marginal case for B011 falls and B005 becomes the stronger configuration.
How much the indirect identification of the collateral channel should count against a foundational theory contribution, compared with the more direct firm-level confirmation of B005.

Whether leaving out Gertler and Gilchrist leaves a real part of the credit-frictions story unrecognised. I judge that a three-name version blurs the mechanism and splits Gertler's credit with B019, but I would not treat that as settled if colleagues argue the strands cannot be separated.
For B005, whether Helpman's marginal credit can be stated independently of the 2008 prize and of B020, and whether wording can avoid overreaching on Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum.
My assessments rely on general knowledge and the supplied committee text. I have not independently verified any literature or source.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Kiyotaki, Moore, Helpman, Melitz or any other credited name on B011, B005 or B001 appears in my supplied profile. I disclose, without adjudicating, that I frequently co-author with Per Krusell (secretary, a B011 supporter), and that I have co-authored with Timo Boppart and Richard Friberg (both B005 supporters). My research is in macroeconomics, so B011 is in an adjacent field. I am also chair and wrote the round 1 chair summary, which synthesised members' positions including my own. Separately, I gave the 2018 presentation speech, and the 2018 Scientific Background cites my own co-authored climate paper. That has no bearing on these candidates. I treat agreement or disagreement with any colleague as no evidence of merit.
